Convert between Unicode encodings

Source: R/convert.R
utf_convert.Rd

utf_convert() converts bytes from one encoding to another. utf_decode() converts bytes to a character vector marked UTF-8. utf_encode() converts a character vector to bytes.

Usage

utf_convert(x, from, to, invalid = c("error", "replace", "na"))

utf_decode(x, from = "auto", invalid = c("error", "replace", "na"))

utf_encode(x, to = "UTF-16LE", invalid = c("error", "replace", "na"))

Arguments

x

For utf_convert() and utf_decode(), a raw vector (one element) or a list of raw vectors (one element each, NULL for a missing one). For utf_encode(), a character vector, taken in its marked encoding; strings marked "bytes" are refused.

from

The encoding of x: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-16", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE", "UTF-32", "Latin-1", or "auto" for utf_detect()'s first candidate (UTF-8 when there is none). Matched without regard to case or hyphens.

to

The target encoding: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE" or "Latin-1".

invalid

"error", "replace" or "na"; see Details.

Value

utf_convert() and utf_encode(): a raw vector for a raw vector or a single string, otherwise a list of raw vectors (NULL for a missing or, under "na", invalid element). utf_decode(): a character vector marked UTF-8, one string per element. A list or a character vector keeps its names.

Details

Every pair of UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 (either byte order) and Latin-1 converts in both directions. A leading byte-order mark that matches from is dropped, and with "UTF-16", "UTF-32" or "auto" it chooses the encoding; the output never carries one.

invalid says what happens to input that is ill-formed in from, and, with a "Latin-1" target, to code points above U+00FF:

  • "error" raises a zuutf_encoding_error with the element's index, the offset of the problem in the input's code units and the encoding it lies in.

  • "replace" writes U+FFFD (or ? in Latin-1, which has no U+FFFD) in place of each maximal ill-formed subpart, as the WHATWG decoder does: one per unpaired surrogate in UTF-16, one per out-of-range unit in UTF-32, one per partial unit at the end, and one per unrepresentable code point.

  • "na" gives NA (NULL in a list of raw vectors) for that element.

R strings cannot hold U+0000, so utf_decode() raises zuutf_nul_error with its index and offset whatever invalid says; utf_convert() keeps it.

See also

utf_detect(), utf_valid(), utf_length_as(); iconv().

Examples

# UTF-16 from a Windows tool, with its byte-order mark
b <- as.raw(c(0xff, 0xfe, 0x63, 0x00, 0x61, 0x00, 0x66, 0x00, 0xe9, 0x00))
utf_decode(b)                          # "auto" reads the BOM
#> [1] "café"
utf_decode(b, "UTF-16LE")
#> [1] "café"

utf_encode("caf\u00e9", "UTF-16BE")
#> [1] 00 63 00 61 00 66 00 e9
utf_convert(charToRaw("caf\u00e9"), "UTF-8", "Latin-1")
#> [1] 63 61 66 e9

# ill-formed input
bad <- as.raw(c(0x61, 0xff, 0x62))
utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8", invalid = "replace")
#> [1] "a�b"
utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8", invalid = "na")
#> [1] NA
tryCatch(
  utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8"),
  zuutf_encoding_error = function(e) e$offset
)
#> [1] 2
utf_encode("\u4e2d", "Latin-1", invalid = "replace")
#> [1] 3f
